summary: Four Node/Playwright test scripts plus a shared helper (t4lib.js). Run each after `bash build.sh` with `node handoff/T4.test.tests/<file>` from the repo root; DIST defaults to ./dist and the page is served at /doom/. They need the `playwright` npm package. They were only syntax-checked (node --check) because emcc and Python playwright are not available locally, so no assertion has executed against a real build. Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 fail, 70 precondition/infra error (for example the player is blocked by a wall). Movement thresholds are derived from direction and sign rather than invented distances. The run test requires the run distance to exceed 1.2x the walk distance over equal tic windows, and the release test compares drift against the held-key rate. Known risk: the dual-Ctrl edge case (EDGE.dual-ctrl) probably fails, because web/doom-boot.js maps ControlLeft and ControlRight to one Doom key but tracks them separately. That is informational, not part of the acceptance text.

tests.purpose: Forward and back move along the facing direction, left and right turn with the correct sign without translating the player, and Control decrements ammo. Also checks for page errors.

Shift+Up covers more distance than walking over the same tic window. Motion stops after keyup compared with a held-key control. Walking speed returns after Shift is released. The tic rate stays within 26.25-43.75 tics/s while a key is held.
On a page made scrollable, arrow and Space keydowns are defaultPrevented and scrollY is unchanged. The canvas keeps focus. A window blur event releases a held key, and keys work again afterwards.
Chorded move plus turn with no prior click. Repeated keydown without keyup does not stick. Left and right Ctrl overlap keeps firing. Unmapped keys are not swallowed. Rapid taps leave no stuck key.
Shared helper that serves dist, launches Chromium, waits for the first tic plus 2 s warmup, and provides state getters from the six DG_TEST hooks and tic-based waiting. Not a test on its own.
